newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: More quakes hit Pakistan, no casualties reported.
newsitem.headline: More quakes hit Pakistan, no casualties reported.

text.p: Two moderate earthquakes jolted two Pakistani towns but caused no casualties on Monday, officials said, three days after a more powerful quake cost about 60 lives in southwestern Pakistan.
The first of Monday's shocks was felt in Sibi, 110 km (69 miles) southeast of Quetta, capital of southwestern Baluchistan province, at 2.29 a.m. (2129 GMT), officials said.

An official at the government seismic centre in the northwestern city of Peshawar measured the tremor at 5.2 on the Richter scale and said its epicentre was in the Harnai district, about 100 km (63 miles) east of Quetta.
Villages in the Harnai area suffered the most casualties and damage in Friday's quake, which also caused deaths in Sibi.

The second of Monday's tremors, measuring 4.5 on the Richter scale, struck Peshawar itself at 11.38 a.m. (0638 GMT). Its epicentre was 130 km (81 miles) southwest of the North West Frontier Province capital, near the border with Afghanistan.
There were no immediate reports of damage from the two latest earthquakes, officials said.
